headline: Two American economists win the Nobel prize in economics
deck: Robert Hall and Michael Woodford are honoured for models that central banks and governments use to smooth out booms and slumps.
standard: Robert E. Hall of Stanford University and Michael Woodford of Columbia University won this year's Nobel prize in economics on Monday, for what the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences called 'microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation'. The two Americans share 12 million Swedish kronor.

Their models show how fiscal and monetary policy can smooth out booms and slumps. John Hassler, who chairs the prize committee, said the winners' work had given 'a solid theoretical foundation for the models that are used today by central banks and governments around the world'.
During the financial crisis of 2008 it shaped central banks' monetary policy.
short: Robert E. Hall of Stanford University and Michael Woodford of Columbia University, both Americans, won the Nobel prize in economics on Monday for models that show how fiscal and monetary policy can smooth out booms and slumps.
Their work shaped central banks' monetary policy during the financial crisis of 2008.
